parsed.explanation: The dossier documents a new criminal statute (in force 13 Dec 2024) carrying 2–5 years' imprisonment for same-sex conduct. It is birth-sex-fixed, so a trans visitor in a relationship read as same-sex, or whose gender-nonconforming presentation draws an arrest on perceived same-sex conduct, falls within it. Pre-existing enforcement of Article 225 and morality laws against gender-nonconforming expression is documented, and reporting describes a qualitative rise in arbitrary arrests and appearance-based physical abuse since the code took effect. The military government justified the code on moral grounds, and the justice minister pledged criminalisation. There is no anti-discrimination law or complaint mechanism, and the 2023 constitution closes partner recognition. Attitude data is old and concerns homosexuality, not trans people, so it is weak evidence. I found no documented trans-specific custody, facility or entry rules, no execution, and no count of the arrest increase. Weighing the documented arrest-and-imprisonment exposure with no recourse, the rating sits in the High Risk band, near the 0.25 anchors for raids and detention. The thin trans-specific record and the absence of documented custody or entry rules keep it above the severe-risk anchors.
